properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: The Scott Lookout Tower is under reconstruction after it burned in the Bovee fire of 2022. Located on a high vantage point, visitors can see for miles. There is a pollinator garden at the base of the tower's hill.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.restrictions: Children under 18 need to be accompanied by an adult.
details.directions: From Thedford, Nebraska, take Highway 2 about 17 miles east and then turn south (right) into the forest onto State Spur 86B.  After crossing the river, stay to the west (right) on State Spur 86B.  Follow 86 B about 3 miles to its end, which is a loop around the tower.

properties.name: NIOBRARA RIVER CANOE LAUNCH
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Located on State Spur 16F at the Niobrara River Bridge, this is a day use site on the Niobrara River for launching small water craft.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.hours: Open 24 / 7 unless closed due to hazardous conditions.
details.directions: From Highway 20, turn south on State Spur 16F at Nenzel and go 9 miles.

properties.name: CLIFFS
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: The Cliffs Trailhead is named for the large cliff face above Bordeaux Creek. It is a popular area for both motorized and non-motorized trail users. The trails are suitable for all levels of riders and hikers. Dispersed camping is allowed. Please recreate responsibly.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.restrictions: Certified noxious weed-free hay is required when enjoying the National Forests on horseback.
details.directions: From Chadron, NE from intersection of Highway 385 and Highway 20, travel 5 miles east on Highway 20 to Bordeaux Road. South 7 miles to Forest Road # 723. West 1.4 miles to Cliffs Trailhead and Picnic Area.

properties.name: HUDSON-MENG
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Located on the beautiful Oglala National Grassland in northwestern Nebraska, Hudson-Meng Bison Bonebed and Visitor Center contains one of the most important paleo-archeological discoveries in North America. Visitors can discover the mysterious past of the ancient bison and explore the prairie of today. Please contact the district office at 308-432-0300 for hours of operation.

details.directions: From Hot Springs, South Dakota : Take Highway 71 south about 60 miles to Toadstool Road. Follow Toadstool Road and Sandcreek Road west about 15 miles.  From Crawford, Nebraska: From the intersection of Highway 20, take Highway 2 north for 5 miles to Toadstool Road.  Follow Toadstool Road and Sandcreek Road west about 15 miles.

properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

There is a shower-house that is only open seasonally. Vault toilets are available year-round. A group site and/or a picnic pavilion is available by reservation. The complex includes an arboretum, fishing pond, picnic tables and river access.

properties.name: TOADSTOOL
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.activities: CAMPING, GENERAL DAY | HIKING | NATURE STUDY | PICNICKING
details.description: Toadstool Geologic Park is a stark, other-worldly landscape unlike any other place in Nebraska. From the small campground, visitors can hike different trails to explore the badlands rock formations and prairie ecosystem. In 1984, the Forest Service constructed a sod house near the site of a former sod house built in 1929.  The new "soddie" provides a look into the past when the homesteaders on the grasslands used the only abundant material available. Fossils and artifacts are protected under federal laws. Please recreate responsibly.

$3 per vehicle per day
Overnight Use:

properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Dismal Trailhead is located near the Bessey Recreation Complex. The Dismal Trail is open to all OHVs 64" or less in width. Truck and trailer parking is available at the trailhead and nearby. Spark arrestors are legally required.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.hours: Open 24 hours/day. Quiet hours 10:00 pm - 8:00 am.
details.directions: located 2 miles west of Halsey and 16 miles east of Thedford, just south of the Bessey Recreation Complex.

properties.name: ROBERTS TRACT
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Roberts Tract Campground and Trailhead provides three camp sites with tables and fire rings, an eight-paddock corral system, rider ramp and stock water. The parking area has one site with a table and fire ring for those with horse trailers or campers. Stock water is available, weather permitting. Roberts Loop Trail (2.5 miles) begins at the campground and provides access to the Pine Ridge National Recreation Area and Pine Ridge Trail.
details.feeDescription:
Overnight Use:
Single Site: $15 per night (1 vehicle include per site)
Additional Vehicle Fee: $7.50 per night
details.hours: Open 24 hours/day. Quiet hours 10:00 pm- 6:00 am.
details.restrictions: Certified noxious weed-free hay/feed is required on national forest lands.  Motorized vehicles are prohibited within Pine Ridge National Recreation Area.
details.directions: From Chadron at the intersection of Highway 385 and Highway 20, southwest on Highway 20, 9.4 miles to Eleson Road. South 3 miles, road jogs .5 miles to the west, then continue south 4 miles to Bethel Road. Follow Bethel Road East 1 mile to Forest Road #737.  Travel on Forest Road #737 for 1 mile to Roberts Tract Campground/Trailhead, just follow the signs to the Pine Ridge National Recreation Area.

properties.name: WHITETAIL
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.activities: CAMPING, GENERAL DAY | HORSEBACK RIDING | PICNICKING | VIEWING WILDLIFE
details.description: Located in the southeastern corner of the Bessey Ranger District on the Dismal River, this campground has a hand pump for water, nine horse corrals, picnic tables, fire rings, and modern vault toilets.  It is situated on the OHV trail system.  No electricity is available. The road to this site is very sandy.
details.feeDescription:
Overnight Use:
Single Site: $15 per night
details.hours: Open 24 hours/day. Quiet hours 10:00 pm - 8:00 am.
details.restrictions: Livestock must be kept and fed in the corrals.  No portable panels or electric fencing are allowed.  Certified weed-free hay is required.  No livestock are allowed in the campground.
details.directions: From Highway 2, turn south into the forest.  After crossing the river, stay right on State Spur 86B.  Follow 86B to Forest Road 203 south (do not turn right at the first 203, take the left up the road).  Follow 203 south about 8 miles to Forest Road 224 east, then follow the signs to the campground.

properties.name: STEER CREEK
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.activities: CAMPING, GENERAL DAY | HIKING | HORSEBACK RIDING | PICNICKING
details.description: Tucked in the shade of ponderosa pines planted in the early 1900's, this 23-unit campground is in the southeast corner of the Samuel R. McKelvie National Forest. A hand water pump, picnic tables, fire rings, and modern vault toilets make this an attractive base from which to explore the Sandhills.  The Blue Jay Trail, a one-mile nature loop, starts and ends at the campground.  For horseback riders, a corral with stalls is available, with a manure bunk nearby.  We ask that horses not be in individual campsites unless being saddled.
details.feeDescription:
Overnight Use:
Single Site: $15 per night
details.hours: Open 24 hours/day. Quiet hours 10:00 pm - 8:00 am.
details.directions: From Highway 20 at Nenzel, go south on State Spur 16F for 18 miles.  The campground will be to the west (right).  From Valentine, head south on Highway 97 for 26 miles, then turn right onto the Merritt Dam Road.  Continue on the Merritt Dam Road (County Road 5) for 15 miles.  At the T, turn left onto at State Spur 16F and go 2 miles to the campground.

properties.name: NATICK
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.activities: CAMPING, GENERAL DAY | HORSEBACK RIDING | PICNICKING | VIEWING WILDLIFE
details.description: The Natick Campground is quieter than the Bessey Recreation Complex, and it has 20 corrals for riding stock.  This 17-unit campground has a hand pump for non-potable water, picnic tables, fire rings, modern vault toilets, and an outstanding view of the night sky.  It is situated on the border of the hand-planted forest and the native grasslands. No OHV riding is allowed from this campground.
details.feeDescription:
Overnight Use:
Single Site: $15 per night
details.hours: Open 24 hours/day. Quiet hours 10:00 pm - 8:00 am.
details.restrictions: Livestock must be fed certified weed-free hay.  Livestock must be kept in the corrals; portable panels and electric fencing are not allowed.  Livestock are not allowed to be in campsites, except for saddling and unsaddling (no more than 30 minutes).  Please clean the corrals after use with the wheelbarrow provided and deposit manure in the bunk.  Please do not let your dog swim or bathe in the windmill tank as it is there to water the livestock.
details.directions: From Thedford, Nebraska: Take Highway 2 east about 17 miles to the forest entrance.  At the national forest sign, turn south (right) onto State Spur 86B. Stay on State Spur 86B west for about 1.5 miles, then take Forest Road 212 about 7 miles to the campground.

details.description: The Soldier Creek Campground is adjacent to Soldier Creek Wilderness Area and Fort Robinson State Park. There is a hand pump well providing drinking water, vault toilets, garbage cans and a large 15-paddock corral system with a round pen.  Livestock feed is not available. Certified weed-free hay is required, and stock water must be hauled to the corral from nearby creeks or hand pump.
